item.title: Industrial Organization and Economics for Competition Policy and Regulation
item.content:encoded:
Managerial and Decision Economics is establishing special sections dedicated to industrial organization and regulatory economics. The initiative welcomes both theoretical and empirical research exploring various dimensions of these fields from international scholars and research students.

The call has no submission deadline and will remain open indefinitely, with accepted manuscripts compiled into a special section. Submissions from industrial and regulatory economics as well as related disciplines are encouraged and should be made through the MDE portal.

Appel publié par Managerial and Decision Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Industrial organization
  • Economics for competition policy
  • Regulatory economics
  • Theoretical work in industrial and regulatory economics
  • Empirical work in industrial and regulatory economics

item.title: Moral Adaptation, Business Strategy, and Innovation
item.content:encoded:
Shanyong Wang, University of Science and Technology of China

Liang Wan, University of Science and Technology of China

Jun Li, Hefei University of Technology

The COVID-19 pandemic and climate disasters have revealed the limitations of market-based institutions and governments in managing systemic crises. This has prompted increased attention to corporate moral motivation and business ethics as essential for sustainable development. The special issue examines how moral adaptation, business strategy, and innovation interconnect in addressing global challenges.

The relationship between these dimensions is complex. Moral evolution and environmental justice reshape corporate strategy, yet traditional economic theory struggles to reconcile justice with efficiency and ethics with innovation. Simultaneously, businesses play an increasingly vital role in developing solutions to major societal problems, including climate change, through strategic adaptation that affects both their operations and their broader ecosystems.

The special issue calls for research reconsidering business ethics in light of contemporary environmental and social concerns. It welcomes global submissions exploring how ethics, institutional frameworks, and innovation interact to support sustainable business practices and address grand challenges.

Potential topics

  • Neuro-economic foundation of ethics and the future development in business ethics
  • Ethics, culture/institutions, and sustainable development
  • Ethics, culture/institutions, and innovation
  • Ethics and public good investments, and innovation

item.title: The Economics of Privacy and Platform Competition
item.content:encoded:
Joanna Poyago-Theotoky, University of Salento

Bipasa Datta, University of York

This special issue focuses on the economic dimensions of privacy and data protection in digital markets, particularly those shaped by online platforms. The editors invite theoretical, experimental, and empirical research examining how personal data is valued, protected, and exploited in contemporary digital economies. The collection seeks to advance understanding of the economic mechanisms through which privacy concerns intersect with market competition and consumer behavior.
